gaps: Ministers of state (Campbell era: early childhood development, mental health, intermediate/long-term/home care, women's equality, deregulation, Community Charter, intergovernmental relations, mining, forestry operations, resort development, immigration and multicultural services, women's and seniors' services, childcare, ActNow BC, Olympics, climate action, building code renewal) are omitted by instruction; the LLBC Campbell list has them if needed.

The Premier office itself is omitted; each premier's President of the Council / President of the Executive Council is included, plus Glen Clark's Minister Responsible for Youth and Dan Miller's Energy and Mines and Northern Development portfolios.
Deputy Premier is included, though it heads no ministry.

Handover gaps are a convention of the sources, not vacancies: LLBC ends outgoing ministers on the day the new premier was sworn in (1996-02-22, 2000-02-24), but reappoints them only when the new cabinet was sworn (1996-02-28, 2000-02-29). 1999-08-25 and 2001-06-05 have no such gap.

LLBC (the primary source) leaves out administrative acting designations. The acting records here are: Dan Miller at Small Business, Tourism and Culture (1996-06-26 to 1996-09-03) and Joy MacPhail at Education, Skills and Training and at Labour (1996-12-12 to 1997-01-06), both from LLBC footnotes, and John Cashore at Environment, Lands and Parks (1995-05-05 to 1995-05-10), from Wikipedia only. Cashore overlaps LLBC's Sihota record, which runs to the rescinding OIC dated 1995-05-10.
Art Charbonneau held Forests from 1992-09-17 to 1992-12-16 while Dan Miller was suspended. LLBC records it as an OIC appointment, so acting=false.

Mike (Michael) de Jong was Solicitor General from 2010-04-09 to 2010-05-04 and from 2010-05-05 to 2010-10-25. News reports call this interim, but LLBC lists OIC appointments, so acting=false. Kash Heed's one-day return (2010-05-04 to 2010-05-05) is included.

Harcourt kept responsibility for the BC Trade Development Corporation (per Wikipedia and the Times Colonist). Neither LLBC nor Wikipedia gives it a formal portfolio title or dates, so it is not recorded.
Robin Blencoe was a minister without portfolio from 1995-03-09 to 1995-04-04 (per Wikipedia). Skipped by instruction.

Gordon Wilson's Minister Responsible for the British Columbia Ferry Corporation: the LLBC Clark table ends it on 1999-07-21, but an LLBC footnote says OIC 898/99 continued it. LLBC's Miller list then starts 'Ferries, Minister Responsible for' on 1999-09-21, while Wikipedia says 1999-08-25. So the ferries portfolio is ambiguous from 1999-07-21 to 1999-09-21.

Jan Pullinger's Minister Responsible for Volunteers and the Community Services Sector starts on 1998-04-21 per LLBC, from a news release with no OIC. Wikipedia says 1998-03-21. The LLBC table prints the end date as '199-07-21'; it has been corrected to 1999-07-21.
Ministry of Agriculture and Lands was vacant from 2009-01-20, when Stan Hagen died in office, until Ron Cantelon's appointment on 2009-01-30. No acting minister was found.
Children and Family Development: Gordon Hogg resigned on 2004-01-23, and Christy Clark was appointed on 2004-01-26.
Shirley Bond as Deputy Premier: a news release dates it to September 2004 (LLBC uses 2004-09-20), but the first OIC is dated 2004-12-15.

Naming discrepancies: LLBC has 'Natural Resources Operations' and Wikipedia 'Natural Resource Operations' (the Wikipedia form is used, sourced to Wikipedia). For Ida Chong's 2008-06-23 to 2009-01-19 portfolio, LLBC has 'Technology, Trade and Economic Development' and Wikipedia 'Technology, Trade and the Arts' (LLBC used). Wikipedia styles Dan Miller's-era tourism ministry 'Tourism, Small Business and Culture' where LLBC has 'Small Business, Tourism and Culture' (LLBC used).
Wikipedia starts Ujjal Dosanjh as Harcourt's Minister Responsible for Sports on 1995-04-19; LLBC gives 1995-04-10 (used).
Edward John was not an MLA when appointed Minister of Children and Families (2000-11-01), so party is null.
Names follow LLBC forms (e.g. Michael Farnworth, Michael de Jong, Gordon Hogg, Art Charbonneau, Gretchen Mann Brewin); Wikipedia uses Mike Farnworth, Mike de Jong, Gordie Hogg, Arthur Charbonneau.

Minister Responsible for ICBC (Miller-era LLBC wording) is normalised to 'Minister Responsible for the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia', and 'Public Service' to 'the Public Service'. Other styling varies by era as printed, e.g. 'Co-operatives' in the Clark list vs 'Cooperatives' in the Miller and Dosanjh lists.
